Under 500 g: two holders from one spool

Brian, October 12: keep the filament below 500 g so two holders print from one 1000 g spool. The October 11 file takes 564 g of body PETG (580 g with the support interface and the inlay colour, which come off other spools). Every number on this page is from a real slice of the print file with the X2D's own settings, read back from its G-code.

Where the 564 g goes

The holder itself is 382 g: the solid base and face you asked for (75 and 97 g), the drum's 20% gyroid core (97 g), three walls everywhere (76 g) and the solid layers under the skins (36 g). The other 182 g, a third of the spool, is thrown away after the print: 151 g of tree and block supports in body PETG and the 30 g prime tower the two nozzles swap on. The lip is the big one. Printed plate down, it is a flat shelf 1-1/2 in deep and 4 in across hanging 3-7/8 in above the bed, and the slicer stands a dense comb block under the whole of it (83 g). The cove under the flange gets a ring of trees (46 g) and the cavity's roof its own (22 g).

The levers, each sliced

Everything tried, one change at a time against the October 11 file. The solid base and face stay as they are in every row, and so does the part's shape.

The options

A and B keep Bambu's recommended hybrid supports for this PETG and interface pairing, with the two cheap support changes and a lighter core. C is the lightest file and the one I would not print: slim trees under a shelf 3-7/8 in up.

B: as A with a 10% core465 g481 g8 h 34 min930 g70 g
C: slim one-wall trees, 15% core453 g469 g8 h 38 min906 g94 g

A: the two support changes and a 15% corerecommended

The part is unchanged except the drum's core, 15% gyroid instead of 20%. The lip's block keeps its two-wall perimeter and dense top with the comb at 5 mm, the trees get one wall. 488 g of body PETG, 8 h 55 min. Two holders take 976 g: it fits, with 24 g to spare for the purge line at the start of each print and the spool's own variance. If you want more cushion than that, B.

B: the same with a 10% core

465 g and 8 h 34 min: 70 g left after two holders. The drum's core at 10% is still a gyroid every 6 mm or so between the cavity's walls and the outer skin; the plate, the face and the skins are what take a drop.

C: slim trees, the lightest file

453 g and 8 h 38 min, the lip standing on single-wall slim trees instead of the block. Bambu rates slim trees for small overhangs; this one is a 4 in shelf 3-7/8 in up, in PETG. If a column wobbles or the nozzle catches a branch at hour eight, the lip's underside fails on the spot. Shown because it is the lightest; not recommended.

Not done: the part's shape

The cove under the flange is what the ring of trees holds up, 46 g of it. A flange underside that climbs at 45 degrees instead of curving to flat would print with no ring at all, but it changes the roll from the drum into the face that you asked the base to match. Left alone unless you want it.

Which one: A, B or C?
